newsitem.title: MEXICO: BASEBALL-PUERTO RICO, MEXICO OPEN CARIBBEAN SERIES WITH WINS.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-PUERTO RICO, MEXICO OPEN CARIBBEAN SERIES WITH WINS.

text.p: Heavily favoured Puerto Rico and defending champions Mexico opened the four-nation Caribbean Series baseball championship with victories on Tuesday.

In the series opener, Bob Hamelin drove in four runs on two homers and a RBI single to power Puerto Rico's Indios de Mayaguez (Mayaguez Indians) to a 7-4 victory over the Dominican Republic's Aguilas de Cibao (Cibao Eagles).

In the second game, Guillermo Velazquez belted a two-run homer in the bottom of the seventh to lift Mexico's Tomateros de Culiacan (Culiacan Tomato Growers) to a 3-1 victory over Venezuela's Navegantes de Magallanes (Magellan Navigators).

The series features the professional winter league champions from Puerto Rico, the Dominican Republic, Mexico and Venezuela. Each of the four teams will play the other three twice in a round-robin format to determine the champions.

Hamelin, who plays for the Kansas City Royals, launched a two-run homer in the first inning, drove in a run with a single in the third and hit a solo homer in the sixth to lead the way for the major league talent-laden Puerto Rico team.
Armando Rios added a solo homer off Dominican starter and loser Julian Tavarez of the San Francisco Giants and belted a a two-run double in the top of the ninth.
Left-hander Joe Rosado was credited with the victory for Puerto Rico, giving up one run on five hits over six innings.

Velazquez, Mexico's cleanup hitter who once played in the San Diego Padres organisation, erased a 1-0 deficit with an opposite-field shot to left-centre with one runner aboard that brought the sellout crowd of 15,500 at Hector Espino Stadium to life.
Adan Amezcua added the third run later in the seventh with a RBI single after Venezuela had intentionally walked the previous batter to set up a force.
The game had been a pitchers' duel between Mexico's Martin Hernandez and Venezuela's Juan Francisco Castillo through six innings.
Andy Abad broke the scoreless tie when he doubled home a run for Venezuela in the top of the seventh. But the defending champions erupted for three runs in the bottom of the inning.

Hernandez, who went 5-0 in post-season to help Culiacan win the Mexican Pacific League title, got the victory, yielding six hits in 7-1/3 innings. Juan Jose Lopez retired the final five Venezuela batters for the save.
